sources.title: Didi Java backend interview raw Question list

claims.text: The preserved interview task asks only for three threads alternating Fibonacci output; its source context is Java backend and it does not preserve term count, start convention, method signature, cancellation contract, or performance target.

The candidate uses three Java Semaphore instances as an explicit baton ring so only the current slot advances shared Fibonacci/output state; the Java concurrency specification provides the synchronization/memory-consistency boundary used by the design.
BigInteger supplies arbitrary-precision integer addition so long Fibonacci examples are not constrained by int/long overflow in this candidate.
The exact candidate compiles on Java 21 and repeatedly emits exact Fibonacci values with thread slot index mod 3, completes boundary cases including 200 terms, and terminates all workers.

validation.command: extract exact Java candidate; javac --release 21; timeout 45s java ThreeThreadFibonacciTest
validation.reported_stdout: PASS repeats=300 terms=100 round-robin=T0,T1,T2 fibonacci=exact BigInteger long-case=200 zero-case=empty negative=rejected
checks: thread slot is exactly index mod 3
Fibonacci values match independent BigInteger oracle

boundary_tests.expected: exact values and T0/T1/T2 ownership without hang

findings: The answer keeps the exact source requirement—three threads alternating Fibonacci output—separate from adopted API details such as term count and F(0)=0/F(1)=1.
Java is grounded in the source interview position rather than invented from the short Question wording.
The semaphore baton establishes deterministic T0/T1/T2 ownership without sleep, busy waiting, or scheduler assumptions.
Termination is explicit: after completion the baton is propagated so every blocked worker can observe the stop condition and exit.
The exact Java 21 candidate passes repeated compile/stress validation, round-robin ownership checks, an independent Fibonacci oracle, and boundary cases.
The answer does not fabricate production use or claim that three threads improve this inherently sequential recurrence.
